calls.video_title: 4 AI Stocks to Buy After NVIDIA's $1 Trillion Comeback
calls.thesis: BUY first tracked (collab with The Motley Fool's Neil). Intel is being punished for the right reasons — consumer CPUs ~50% of revenue are weak as memory pricing makes PCs pricier, and the server-CPU supply chain isn't ready for the demand — but CEO Lip-Bu Tan owns the mistake and is fixing it; server-CPU and foundry growth should return in 2-3 quarters, with external foundry customers arriving in H2 next year. Neil: 'more upside than risk from here on out.'
calls.base_case: Supply chain gets fixed and server-CPU/foundry revenue growth resumes over the next 2-3 quarters.
calls.bull_case: Guidance growth returns as the supply chain is fixed and external foundry demand grows.
calls.bear_case: Consumer PC weakness lasts longer and the supply chain stays unready, delaying the recovery.

calls.video_title: Best Semiconductor Stocks to Buy: Micron vs. Intel | MU Stock vs. INTC Stock
calls.thesis: Fairly valued on his DCF ($50 vs $54) and he is 'not interested in owning Intel at anywhere near these market prices' — despite 75%/yr forecast EPS growth and agentic-AI CPU demand. He owns Micron, not Intel.
calls.base_case: CPU demand from agentic AI lifts sales after years of manufacturing investment; branded CPUs growing.
calls.bull_case: Agentic AI improves the GPU/CPU ratio in data centers in Intel's favour; foundry eventually wins third-party customers.
calls.bear_case: Foundry still lacks customers with excess capacity compressing margins; ROIC -7%; government-stake excitement ran ahead of performance.

calls.video_title: Interesting Update for Intel Stock Investors | INTC Stock Deep Dive Part 3
calls.thesis: Fairly valued after the >50% crash from its all-time high: his DCF fair value is $51.37 vs $57.32 market, forward P/E 32 (was 80). Buying at fair value is reasonable; ~$45 would make it undervalued.
calls.base_case: 18A yields improving at a double-digit rate, Nova Lake design wins tracking 2x Panther Lake, agentic AI could grow the server CPU TAM 5x ($40bn to $200bn+ in 5 years).
calls.bull_case: Foundry wins from external customers would use idle capacity and lift margins and cash flow sharply.
calls.bear_case: Still far behind in GPUs and has not yet captured external foundry customers; fair value below the current price.

calls.video_title: Why Is Everyone Talking About Intel Stock? | INTC Stock Deep Dive Part 2
calls.price_at_call: $57.34 (stated current); peaked at $141 earlier this year
calls.fair_value: Below $57.34 — 'still a little bit above the fair value estimate'
calls.thesis: HOLD reiterated — not a buying opportunity just yet, still a little rich even after the fall from $141; valuation is getting closer to his fair value but near-term headwinds keep him waiting for a lower entry.
calls.base_case: CPU demand soaring as agentic AI proliferates; new D-series inference GPU unveiled with encouraging early feedback and customer engagements progressing toward firm commitments; pent-up PC replacement demand keeps growing (2020-21 buyers now in the 4-6 year cycle).
calls.bull_case: If Intel captures even mid-single-digit GPU market share for data centres it would be huge and is not priced in; a PC rebound once memory/storage component prices normalise releases the coiled-spring pent-up demand.
calls.bear_case: Israel factory accident shuts output and hits Q4 10nm server products; PC correction accelerating as partners manage inventory down and consumers balk at higher prices — no rebound in H1 2027, probably not in 2027 at all.

calls.video_title: What's Going on With Intel Stock? | INTC Stock Deep Dive Part 1
calls.thesis: HOLD reiterated — not a buying opportunity just yet, but getting much closer; fairly valued after the fall from $133, forward P/E 32 vs ~80 earlier in the year.
calls.base_case: Valuation now close to prospects; 18A Clearwater Forest shipping for revenue, demand for 2027 significant.
calls.bull_case: AI demand and supply expansion lift earnings back toward the growth the market once priced in.
calls.bear_case: Supply shortages and rising capex commitments persist; rivals Micron and TSMC are sold out while Intel is not.

calls.video_title: Why Is Intel Stock Crashing, and is it a Buying Opportunity? | INTC Stock Analysis
calls.thesis: Reiterated hold: 30% post-earnings drop is not yet a buying opportunity; 2027 will be another negative-free-cash-flow investment year and PC demand stays weak into H1 2027.
calls.base_case: Updated DCF intrinsic value $51 vs $64 market price = still overvalued; forward PE 29 reasonable only on expected data-center EPS growth.
calls.bull_case: Data-center demand (>$200B addressable, growing with agentic AI) plus possible Intel Foundry customer announcement could lift it once the business catches up.
calls.bear_case: 2027 CapEx surge with negative FCF, Q4 revenue guided down sequentially to $15.5B with margins falling to 37% from 43%.
